bullets: Most mystery creaks are solved by cleaning contact surfaces and re-torquing to spec; the pattern held across three different teams working with Spoke & Wrench and Shimano.
Chain wear is the single best leading indicator of how soon cassettes will need replacing, which makes it the metric worth watching rather than waiting for a cassette to fail.
Suspension service intervals are a risk-management decision rather than a routine chore, and ignoring them means rebuilding the suspension from scratch a year later.
A bike should feel quiet and predictable so the rider's attention stays on the trail; internalizing that goal makes the rest of the maintenance decisions easier.
Framing maintenance through these principles matters because it reveals which trade-offs are being made, and the second-order effects are the part most people miss.
Risk management cross-cuts every drivetrain and maintenance decision, from creak diagnosis to service scheduling.
Practical adoption starts small: pick one idea, such as chain-wear checks or re-torquing to spec, run it for two weeks, and iterate from there.
